$description: Canonical radius source. Hand-edit this file only; dist/ is generated.

meta.note: Eight values, measured across ALL FOUR content artboards. The first pass swept only D5-0 (the app screens) and so missed 6px and 14px entirely, and wrongly recorded 8px as incidental. These are not a scale - 5, 6, 8, 10, 14, 18, 24 have no consistent ratio - so they are named by pixel value, as spacing is. The two exceptions are `pill` and `full`, which name a shape intent rather than a size.
meta.coverage: D5-0 (light app), 3JI-0 (dark app), 1O8-0 (light showcase), 2LV-0 (dark showcase). 12px, 16px, 20px and 32px are confirmed absent.

5.usage: Checkboxes, and nothing else. The only square-ish control in the system.

6.usage: Chart bars. Used on the weekday bars of the activity charts; ~28 occurrences, all in data visualisation.

8.usage: Small tiles: colour swatches, compact grid cells. Widely used on the showcase boards - the first extraction called this incidental, which was wrong.

10.usage: Inner tiles inside a card: transaction icon squares, stat blocks.

14.usage: 40x40 icon tiles, small bordered cards, chart tooltips, and 24px icon buttons. At 40px this reads as a rounded square rather than a circle, which is what distinguishes it from `pill`.

pill.usage: Every interactive control - buttons, inputs, textareas, badges, tabs, switches, slider tracks and thumbs. At the system's control heights (20/28/32px) 18px exceeds half the height, so it renders as a true pill. This is the system's defining shape; anything else on a control will look wrong.

24.usage: Cards, panels, sheets, dialogs. The outer container radius.

full.usage: Circles: radio dots, avatars, status dots.

controlHeights.$note: Observed alongside the radii. Not yet tokens, but they are what makes 18px read as a pill.
